2. Overview
2.1. Vehicle Overview
Electric Vehicle Ownership
Your vehicle is powered by electricity and as a result some
of the vehicle’s systems and operating characteristics are
different from a vehicle powered by an internal combustion
engine.

different from a vehicle powered by an internal combustion
engine.
It is important to carefully review this entire Owner’s Manual
for this reason. The vehicle does not require and it is not
capable of using gasoline like a vehicle powered by a
traditional internal combustion engine.
The vehicle uses two types of batteries. One is a 12V (low
voltage) battery that is the same as the battery in vehicles
that operate on gasoline powered engines, the other is the

that operate on gasoline powered engines, the other is the
Li-ion battery which may be referred to as the High Voltage
(HV) or Electric Vehicle (EV) battery in this Owner’s Manual.
The 12V battery provides power to the vehicle systems and
features such as the infotainment system, supplemental
restraint systems, headlights and windshield wipers.
The vehicle uses energy stored in the lithium ion (“Li-ion”)
battery. The vehicle’s Li-ion battery must be charged with

battery. The vehicle’s Li-ion battery must be charged with
electricity before the vehicle can be driven. As the vehicle
operates, the Li-ion battery gradually discharges. If the Li-ion
battery becomes completely discharged, the vehicle will not
operate until it is re-charged.
The high voltage Li-ion battery or EV Battery provides power
to the electric motor that drives the vehicle. The vehicle must
be plugged in for the Li-ion battery to be charged.

be plugged in for the Li-ion battery to be charged.
Your vehicle is also equipped with a regenerative braking
system which allows the vehicle to convert kinetic energy
into electrical energy, which is used to recharge the battery
increasing overall range.
This vehicle is considered to be an environmentally friendly
vehicle because it does not emit exhaust gases, such as
carbon dioxide and nitrogen oxide when in operation.

Central Locking  Overview
The vehicle is equipped with a central locking system that
allows all doors and tailgate to be locked and unlocked at
once. Central locking and unlocking of the vehicle can be
accomplished by any of the following:
Vehicle key fob
Keyless entry (ensure the key fob is within 1m of the
vehicle)
Mechanical key
Interior central locking button
Remote locking feature within the VinFast App  (when
available)

Interior central locking button
Remote locking feature within the VinFast App  (when
available)
Details on each of the above features can be found further in
this section.
Interior Central Locking Button
The central locking button
is located in the center console. The central locking button
locks or unlocks all doors and the liftgate when pressed. The
button will illuminate to indicate the vehicle is locked.

How It Works
After the driver’s door has been opened and then
closed, the system will start searching for the keyfob.
If the keyfob remains within the passive entry detection
range (approximately 1 m around the vehicle), the turn
signal will ﬂash to indicate that the Walk-away Lock
feature is ready.

signal will ﬂash to indicate that the Walk-away Lock
feature is ready.
A countdown timer will then start. When the keyfob
moves outside the detection range, the system will
automatically lock all doors and the trunk.

Level I : The vehicle is supplied with a Level 1 charging cable. The vehicle can be charged from grounded household
sockets using Level 1 cables. A household socket connection charges with alternating current. In the case of Level 1

charging cables, the efﬁciency values may differ from those on the energy label.

stations. The charging at Level 2 stations is performed using alternating current. Charging can be completed much faster at
a charging station rather than at a household socket.
Level III : DC charging stations are equipped with a permanent DC charging cable, which makes charging possible.

Charging is carried out at DC charging stations using direct current. A DC charger station with a higher current connection
charges more quickly than a household socket or a Level 2 charging station.

Adaptive Cruise Control Modes
Follow Mode:
When Follow Mode is active, the ACC system will detect a leading vehicle with a speed lower than the ACC set speed.
In follow mode, ACC will adjust the vehicle speed according to the relative distance and relative speed of the detected leading

vehicle. If another vehicle happens to cut in front and reduce this distance , ACC will apply brakes to slow the vehicle speed and
reestablish a safe following distance.
ACC will also adjust the following distance or gap to the vehicle in front based on changes to the driver’s preferred gap setting.
Corner Limit Mode:
Corner Limit Mode limits vehicle acceleration in a corner based on detected lateral acceleration, yaw rate and driving speed to

ensure vehicle traction and stability through a bend.
Overtaking Mode:
When following a leading vehicle, ACC may detect that the driver wishes to overtake the vehicle in front when the turn indicator
is selected. Once detected ACC will then accelerate and allow the gap to the vehicle in front to momentarily decrease. This
allows for a quick and safe overtaking manoever and the set gap setting and vehicle speed will be restored once overtaking is
complete.

Automatic Emergency Braking (AEB) can automatically detect an imminent forward or rearward collision and activate the

the ability to detect other vehicles, motorcycles and vulnerable road users such as pedestrians and cyclists.

The AEB consist of the following types based on the target area:
Front Automatic Emergency Braking
Rear Automatic Emergency Braking

speed of various types of objects on the vehicle’s forwarding trajectory such as other vehicles, motorcycles, pedestrians,
cyclists.

of various types of objects on the vehicle’s reversing trajectory such as pedestrians, roadblocks, pillars.

6.10. Cold Weather
Cold Weather
Overview
Winter months and lower temperatures may cause some
changes in the operation of the vehicle. It is important to be
aware of the effects of cold weather so that you can prepare
accordingly. When snow and ice accumulate on the vehicle,
the battery, tires, wiper ﬂuid, and wipers can freeze. To

the battery, tires, wiper ﬂuid, and wipers can freeze. To
achieve maximum range and performance, it is helpful to
warm the cabin and battery before driving.
When battery is in cold condition, a snowﬂake icon appears
beside battery capacity bar. Battery capacity bar also
changes to amber color.
Impact of cold weather
Battery at risk:
Temperatures lower than -30°C ( -22 °F ) can cause issues
to the battery in terms of performance and range. It is

to the battery in terms of performance and range. It is
recommended to select ECO drive mode to help extend the
range when driving in cold weather.
Frozen Door Handles, Windows, Mirrors:
In winter conditions, snow or ice may buildup within the door
handles, windows and vehicle mirrors. It prevents the
vehicle door, window and mirror from operating properly.
Doors:
1. Apply some extra force while pulling on the door
handles to break it free of ice.

Doors:
1. Apply some extra force while pulling on the door
handles to break it free of ice.
2. Open and close the door handle a few more times to
release any remaining ice buildup.
3. Ensure the door handle is fully retracted before entering
the vehicle, and ensure that the door is fully closed
before you drive off.
Windows:
See > Climate Control System > Front Windscreen Defrost
and Defog and see > Climate Control System > Rear Demist
Alternatively, the VinFast App can be used to defrost the

Alternatively, the VinFast App can be used to defrost the

Mirrors:

mirrors. Therefore, it is recommended to turn OFF Mirror
Auto Fold so that they do not fold when the vehicle is locked.
See > Mirrors > Side Mirrors.
Tire inﬂation issues:
Fluctuating temperatures have impacts on the level of
inﬂation in tires, which makes it extremely important to check

inﬂation in tires, which makes it extremely important to check
the tire pressures frequently in cold conditions. Use winter
tires to increase traction in snowy or icy conditions. See >
Wheels and Tires > Tire Pressure.
Frozen windshield wipers:
Cold temperatures can also cause your windshield wipers to
freeze, which can be dangerous. If snow or ice is expected
when parked, consider tilting the windshield wipers up.
Lighting operation:
Remove any snow, frost or ice that may cover the indicators,

Lighting operation:
Remove any snow, frost or ice that may cover the indicators,

While Driving
Cold conditions increase energy consumption due to more
power which is needed for driving, cabin heating, and
battery charging. Energy consumption can be reduced by
following these tips:
To keep warm, use seat heaters. Seat heaters are less
energy-consuming than cabin heaters. Reducing cabin

energy-consuming than cabin heaters. Reducing cabin
temperature and using seat heaters reduces energy
consumption. See > Climate Controls.
Maintain slow and steady speed while driving and avoid
rapid braking and accelerations.

The HV battery is maintenance free. Always pay attention to the battery status and never allow it to fully discharge. Even when

cold weather), conﬁguration, and selected settings. If the vehicle is not used for long periods of time (approx. 2-3 weeks),
ensure that the vehicle’s HV battery is always above 30% (preferable between 30% to 60%).
